=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:2532-2544 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The merge_with_followup path extracts Tracking issue and Integration branch declarations from unfiltered FIRST_ISSUE_LINEAGE_BODY, allowing fenced or diagnostic content to supply authoritative lineage.
  WHY: The declarations are matched without fence filtering, so an untrusted parent issue can redirect follow-up tracking or branch lineage.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:2546-2567 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Parent branch metadata can suppress the PR-base fallback, including when the parent declares the `(default branch)` sentinel.
  WHY: The modified tests expect the independently verified PR base to win, but the current code clears the sentinel and blocks fallback; this is also the highest severity reported.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:2894-2918 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The close_and_reissue path extracts orchestrator metadata from the full, unfiltered FIRST_ISSUE_LINEAGE_BODY, allowing a fenced block to supply a forged Local ID.
  WHY: Matching tracking and branch declarations do not prevent fenced metadata from carrying a forged Local ID through reissue; all reviewers reporting severity rated this a blocker.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:2584, 2939-2956 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The merge_with_followup path does not strip judge-provided canonical lineage from FOLLOWUP_BODY, and close_and_reissue stripping does not account for fence context.
  WHY: Canonical lines in judge prose or fenced content can remain or be extracted as authoritative lineage.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:2789 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The footer check counts backtick and tilde fences interchangeably instead of tracking the active delimiter.
  WHY: A different delimiter inside an open fence can change the parity count and make a fenced metadata footer appear authoritative.
- scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh:26 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The footer check counts backtick and tilde fences interchangeably instead of tracking the active delimiter.
  WHY: A different delimiter inside an open fence can change the parity count and make a fenced metadata footer appear authoritative.
- scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh:55, 111 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Both embedded extractors count backtick and tilde fences interchangeably instead of tracking the active delimiter.
  WHY: Mixed delimiters can expose a tracking issue number inside an open fence and trigger an unintended force-tick dispatch.
- .github/workflows/validate.yml:217-218 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The authoritative_lines jq function counts backtick and tilde fences interchangeably instead of tracking the active delimiter.
  WHY: A different delimiter inside an open fence can make a fenced metadata footer pass the outside-fence check.
- tests/test_review_rb_judge_label_propagation.py:2505-2562, 782-802 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The modified tests assert lineage filtering and PR-base behavior that the unchanged production code does not implement.
  WHY: The tests exercise behavior absent from scripts/review_rb_judge.sh and will fail against the current implementation; severity ranged from MAJOR to BLOCKER, and the highest is reported.
- tests/test_review_rb_judge_label_propagation.py:2505 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The test name says parent metadata wins over the PR base, while its docstring and assertions expect the PR base to win.
  WHY: The contradictory name misstates the behavior verified by the test.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:2546-2548, 2555-2567 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The default-branch sentinel handling does not clear other rendered default-branch aliases from Target branch declarations.
  WHY: A `Target branch: (default)` alias could survive the sentinel guard and block the PR-base fallback.
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:573-576 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The observed_sha validation calls `.get` on branch before verifying that branch is a dictionary, so a ReadError or other unexpected response shape raises AttributeError.
  WHY: The added test expects a structured exit-2 result, but this path can raise an unhandled exception instead.

- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:2532-2544 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The merge_with_followup path searches the unfiltered FIRST_ISSUE_LINEAGE_BODY for tracking and integration branch declarations using re.search with re.MULTILINE.
  WHY: Fenced diagnostic content containing matching declarations is treated as authoritative lineage and can redirect the follow-up issue to an attacker-controlled branch.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:2894-2918 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The close_and_reissue path searches the full FIRST_ISSUE_LINEAGE_BODY for the first "Orchestrator metadata" line without excluding fenced content.
  WHY: A fenced block with matching tracking and branch values can carry a forged Local ID into reissue metadata.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:2789 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The authoritative metadata footer check sums backtick and tilde delimiter counts together, treating the two delimiter types interchangeably.
  WHY: A different delimiter inside an open fenced block can make a subsequent metadata line appear outside the fence.
- scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh:26 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The footer check sums backtick and tilde delimiter counts together, treating the two delimiter types interchangeably.
  WHY: A tilde line inside a backtick fence can make a footer appear authoritative.
- scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh:55, 111 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Both inline scripts use sum(bool(re.match(r"^(?:```|~~~)", ...))) to extract tracking issue numbers.
  WHY: Mixed delimiter types can expose a tracking issue number that triggers an unintended force-tick dispatch.
- .github/workflows/validate.yml:217-218 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The authoritative_lines jq function counts backtick and tilde fence delimiters together to decide whether the footer is outside a fence.
  WHY: A different delimiter inside an open fenced block can cause its branch declaration to be accepted.
- tests/test_review_rb_judge_label_propagation.py:2505-2562, 782-802 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Tests added in the last run assert PR-base-derived lineage and fenced-content rejection, but scripts/review_rb_judge.sh was not modified.
  WHY: The modified assertions test security hardening the production code never received and will fail against the current code.

  WHY: The misleading name contradicts the test assertions.
